title: Odile and the Escarpment
premise: Desert ranger Ansel Ravensworth is chasing a thief named Odile across the salt flats when a flash flood uncovers a chest bearing the seal of Vessia, a drowned nation everyone thought was legend. The chest holds half of a salvage manifest pointing to a wreck beneath the escarpment, and both the crown's salvage fleet and Odile's outlaw family want it. As Ansel and Odile are forced to travel together, his duty to the law and her debt to her people collide, and they discover the manifest's true cargo: proof that the crown engineered Vessia's flooding and owes reparations to its scattered survivors. Racing the fleet by six tides before the dry season strands them, they reach the wreck, expose the truth, and choose each other over their old allegiances — Ansel burning his ranger's commission, Odile claiming justice not as theft but as inheritance.
about_author: Theo Delacroix is the pen name of a former river surveyor who spent a decade mapping forgotten waterways before turning to fiction. They write adventure stories about borders, debts, and the people who live in the gaps between laws.

chapters.title: The Man Who Chased Nothing
chapters.summary: Ansel Ravensworth, POV. Tracking a thief across the empty flats, Ansel reflects on the debt he owes his dead captain and the commission that keeps him alive. He nearly catches his quarry at dusk, but she vanishes into a dry wash. Emotional beat: lonely resolve hardening into obsession.

chapters.title: What the River Gave Up
chapters.summary: Ansel, POV. A flash flood traps him overnight; at dawn he finds a waterlogged chest stamped with Vessia's seal, and inside, half a salvage manifest. The thief reappears — not fleeing him but staring at the chest in shock. Emotional beat: wonder cracking through professional suspicion.

chapters.title: Odile
chapters.summary: Odile, POV. She reveals her name and her stake: the manifest matches a story her grandmother told about the drowned fleet. She offers a truce — the chest for her freedom. Ansel refuses, but neither can carry it alone through bandit country. Emotional beat: wary bargain struck between enemies.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Ansel, POV. A passing trader warns that the crown's salvage fleet has already launched, and the dry season will drop the river too low to dive within six tides. Ansel does the arithmetic: walking is faster than sailing if they cut the escarpment. Emotional beat: dread converting hesitation into commitment.

chapters.title: The Toll Bridge
chapters.summary: Odile, POV. At a toll bridge, a fleet scout recognizes the Vessian seal and demands the chest. Odile talks them past with a forged writ, revealing talents that unsettle Ansel. That night he asks what else she's stolen. Emotional beat: attraction shadowed by doubt.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Map
chapters.summary: Odile, POV. In an abandoned waystation, Odile deciphers the manifest using songs her grandmother taught her — the cargo list is written as verse. It names a second half-manifest aboard the wreck itself. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into purpose; her inheritance becomes real.

chapters.title: Rangers on the Road
chapters.summary: Ansel, POV. Two fellow rangers catch up, ordered to retrieve Ansel and arrest the thief. He stalls them with a false report, committing his first true act against the law. Emotional beat: guilt and exhilaration entwined; the line crossed cannot be uncrossed.

chapters.title: The Escarpment Path
chapters.summary: Odile, POV. The cliff trail is washed out; they rope down together and a near-fall forces raw honesty — she confesses she stole from Ansel's garrison originally to buy her family's passage papers. Emotional beat: trust earned in danger, secrets spent like coin.

chapters.title: Fleet Smoke
chapters.summary: Ansel, POV. From a ridge they see the fleet anchoring downstream — the scouts found another route. A captured fleet deserter reveals the admiral knows what the wreck carries and means to bury it. Emotional beat: the race becomes a moral one, not just a physical one.

chapters.title: Salt Fever
chapters.summary: Odile, POV. Ansel collapses with fever from a rope-cut wound. Odile nurses him through two tides, losing precious time, and reads aloud from the verse-manifest while he sleeps. Emotional beat: love admitted silently, in care rather than words.

chapters.title: The Drowned Chapel
chapters.summary: Ansel, POV. Sheltering in a half-submerged Vessian chapel, they find carved names of the flooded dead — including Odile's family name. Ansel realizes his own grandfather signed the evacuation order. Emotional beat: shared history revealed as complicity and wound alike.

chapters.title: Turncoat Tide
chapters.summary: Odile, POV. The deserter betrays their position to the fleet for amnesty. They escape a night raid, but the chest is cracked open in the scramble and the verse-manifest is soaked. Emotional beat: fury and fear; the stakes turn personal and irreversible.

chapters.title: Two Tides Left
chapters.summary: Ansel, POV. With the river falling fast, they abandon the safe route for a dangerous shortcut through sinking mudflats. Ansel offers Odile the chance to walk away with her life; she refuses. Emotional beat: devotion declared plainly at last, against all prudence.

chapters.title: The Admiral's Offer
chapters.summary: Odile, POV. Fleet outriders intercept them; Admiral Corvane offers Odile full pardon and her family's papers if she surrenders the manifest and testifies that Ansel went rogue alone. Emotional beat: temptation measured against love; duty weaponized.

chapters.title: One Tide
chapters.summary: Ansel, POV. They reach the wreck site as the water drops to diving depth. Ansel dives despite his healing wound, guided by Odile's sung verses, and finds the sealed strongroom — and the second half of the manifest fused to a ledger of the crown's deliberate sluice-gate orders. Emotional beat: awe and horror in equal measure.

chapters.title: Corvane's Net
chapters.summary: Odile, POV. The fleet surrounds the shallows. Corvane offers Ansel reinstatement and erasure of his debt if he hands over the ledger; Ansel instead burns his commission in front of the assembled crews. Emotional beat: climax of identity — choosing conscience over rank.

chapters.title: The Reading
chapters.summary: Ansel, POV. Cornered on the wreck's exposed hull, Odile stands before the fleet sailors — many descended from Vessian survivors themselves — and sings the manifest verses aloud. Sailors begin refusing orders. Emotional beat: justice outside the law igniting from below.

chapters.title: Mutiny at Low Water
chapters.summary: Odile, POV. Half the fleet turns; Corvane attempts to destroy the ledger and is stopped by his own first officer. Ansel takes a blade meant for Odile. Emotional beat: sacrifice and chaos, love proven in blood.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Tides
chapters.summary: Ansel, POV. Wounded but alive, Ansel wakes as the surviving officers agree to carry the ledger to the capital courts. Corvane is held for trial by his own crew. Emotional beat: exhaustion laced with fragile hope.

chapters.title: Papers
chapters.summary: Odile, POV. The manifest's final page lists survivor families owed reparations — hers among them. Odile signs her true name for the first time in years, no longer a thief but a claimant. Emotional beat: identity restored; the debt of generations acknowledged.

chapters.title: The Escarpment at Dawn
chapters.summary: Ansel, POV. Commissionless and debt-free, Ansel stands where the chase began. Odile joins him; they decide to walk the escarpment together, mapping the drowned villages so the dead are counted. Emotional beat: quiet joy, love chosen freely after duty falls away.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Shared epilogue, alternating voices. Months later, the trial verdict reaches them by courier; reparations begin, imperfectly. On the riverbank, they bury the emptied chest beside the chapel names. Emotional beat: peace without forgetting — the river gives, and the living remember.
